newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Rate fears spook eurobourses after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Rate fears spook eurobourses after U.S. data.

text.p: Leading European shares and Wall Street skidded lower on Friday after U.S. jobs data signalled credit may have to be tightened to prevent the world's powerhouse economy from overheating.

Bourses and currency trading had been marking time ahead of Washington's announcement that 262,000 jobs were created outside the farm sector in December. Wall Street economists had on average forecast only 192,000 jobs would be created.
The closely-watched figures followed a string of data pointing to a strengthening U.S. economy, making an early hike in interest rates by the U.S. Federal Reserve more likely.

Major European bourses had, with the exception of Frankfurt, been nervously lower with sentiment undermined by another big Tokyo share selloff overnight. They fell sharply after the U.S. data, with London, Paris and the German post bourse electronic indices all down over one percent.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average, which rallied to a new record closing high on Thursday, was also spooked by the inflation spectre and tumbled by one percent within minutes of opening. U.S. Treasury bonds were also hit with the benchmark 30-year bond down well over a point.
The effect on the dollar was less clear cut, though it was off its lows in afternoon European trade having moved within a narrow range against the mark and the yen for most of the day.

Earlier, the bloodletting overnight on the Tokyo stock market, where Japanese shares plummeted again after a week of furious selling, had paradoxically softened the dollar against the yen. Analysts said the perception was that the stock freefall may prompt a repatriation of Japanese funds to cover share losses.

In other currency developments, the mark weakened sharply against many other European currencies, plunging to its lowest level against the Norwegian crown for more than four years and eroding key levels against the Spanish peseta.

The backdrop of weak German economic data released on Thursday helped to push the mark lower, while the apparent halting of intervention by the central banks of Norway and Spain sped up the decline, analysts said.
Shortly after Wall Street opened, London, Europe biggest bourse, was down 50 points or 1.2 percent at the day's nadir.
"The nonfarm payrolls were a bit of a shock, there is no doubt about it," said one senior sales trader,

He added that fears of a rise in British interest rates, coupled with a string of downgrades on UK company earnings because of recent sterling strength, made for a gloomy outlook for the London market.

Despite fears that interest rates on both sides of the atlantic were set to rise, a slim majority of analysts polled by Reuters believed U.K. rates would remain unchanged at six percent after next week's monetary meeting between Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George.

A mixed distributive trades survey from the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) on Friday added to London's gloom, with the CBI reporting that clothing, footwear, drugstores and durable goods retailers had a poor December.

In Frankfurt German shares fall sharply in line with the debt market after the U.S. jobs data. The IBIS DAX index of electronic trading was 1.2 percent down by 1445 GMT. Earlier the DAX index of floor trading in Frankfurt had closed at record high before Wall Street opened.
It was a similar story in Paris were French shares doubled their losses after the U.S. figures and the CAC-40 blue chip index was down 1.1 percent by 1445 GMT.
CURRENCIES AT 1445 GMT
The dollar was trading at 115.50 yen and 1.5785 marks compared with 116.20 yen and 1.5775 marks late in Europe on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1445 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was down 45.2 points at 4,041.8.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was down 25.13 at 2,323.95.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 40.76 at 2,933.39 but the IBIS DAX of electronic trading was down 28.99 points at 2,907.7.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was at $359.35 compared with its London close of $355.75 on Thursday. Silver was at $4.76.
